summary: Victoria Sujata is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD at Harvard University, where she studied under Michael Aris.

Vidhusekhara Bhattacharya (1878–1954) worked in Indology and Buddhist studies. He held posts at Visva-Bharati University as a pandit and supervisor of collation (attested 1929–1932) and principal (attested 1944), and served as Asutosh Professor of Sanskrit at the University of Calcutta (attested 1943).
Vidya Dehejia (b. 1942) works in history, archaeology, Indology, and Buddhist studies. She studied at the University of Cambridge (~1961–1968) and held a post at Columbia University around 1982.

Vidya Niwas Mishra (1926–2005) was a scholar in linguistics and Indology. He studied at the University of Allahabad (~1943–1947) and Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Gorakhpur University (~1958–1960), later serving as Professor of Linguistics at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (~1968–1986).

Vilhelm Thomsen (1842–1927) was a linguist and scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Randers State School and the University of Copenhagen (~1859–1869), where he later served as professor (~1887–1913).
Vincent Arthur Smith (1848–1920) worked in Indology, history, and archaeology. He served in the Indian Civil Service (~1871–1900) and held a post at the University of Oxford (~1910–1920).

Vincent Breugem (b. 1970) specializes in Japanology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Leiden University (MA, PhD 2012), Taisho, Hanazono, and Kyoto universities, and under Lucia Dolce. He served as a research fellow at Leiden University (attested 2012).

Vincent Eltschinger (b. 1970) specializes in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. Educated at Collège Saint-Michel and the University of Lausanne (licence 1995, PhD 2003), he held posts at the Austrian Academy of Sciences, University of Vienna, and École Pratique des Hautes Études.

Vincent Goossaert (b. 1969) is a scholar of Sinology, religious studies, and history. He studied under Kristofer Schipper (~1992–1997) and held posts at the CNRS (~1998–2012), The Chinese University of Hong Kong, and École Pratique des Hautes Études (~2012).

Vincent Lefèvre specializes in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at the École Nationale des Chartes and Sorbonne Nouvelle University (HDR 2007), and served as a curator at the Musée Guimet.

Vincent Tournier specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (PhD 2012) and Leiden University, was mentored by Seishi Karashima, and held a post at the École française d'Extrême-Orient (attested 2021).
Vincenzo Vergiani works in Indology and linguistics. He studied under Raffaele Torella and held a post at the University of Cambridge around 2009.
Vindhyeshwari Prasad Dube was an Indologist who held posts at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, attested in 1920 and 1939.

Virendra Nath Misra (1935–2015) was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at Savitribai Phule Pune University (~1958–1961) and served as Director of the Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute (~1993–2000).
Vishwa Nath Pathak (1926–2003) specialized in Indology, history, and archaeology. He held posts at Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Gorakhpur University, attested in 1978 and as professor in 1987.
Vishwanath Prasad Varma (b. 1924) works in philosophy and Indology. He studied under Dhirendra Mohan Datta, Ganga Nath Bhattacharya, Kalikinkar Datta (~1947–1950), and Joachim Wach (1950).
Vitus Angermeier is an Indologist who studied under Chlodwig H. Werba, Roque Mesquita, and Karin Preisendanz (MA supervisor until 2007).

Vladimir Tikhonov (b. 1973) works in history, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He studied at St. Petersburg University, Korea University, and under Kwang Cho, Chul-hwan Chung, and Mikhail Nikolaevich Pak, later becoming a professor at the University of Oslo (~2001).

Vladimir Vyacheslavovich Balabushevich (1900–1970) worked in Indology, history, and archaeology. He served as Head of the Indian Department at the Institute of Oriental Studies of the Russian Academy of Sciences (attested 1970 and 1990).
Volkbert Näther is an Indologist who studied under doctoral supervisor Claus Vogel and earned his doctorate at the University of Marburg (attested 1975).
